title: Fusion CAM API Surface + Cloud Library + HTTP Resilience
brief: Build the foundation for PRISM AutoProgram: CAM setup/operation creation endpoints, B-Rep geometry extraction, Fusion 360 cloud library access, HTTP bridge hardening. This unblocks the entire AutoProgram pipeline (F360-AP-MS1 through MS8).

context_for_cold_start.what_is_this: PRISM AutoProgram is a one-button automated CNC programming system inside Fusion 360. It chains 20+ existing PRISM engines through a 10-stage pipeline: Model Intake → Feature Recognition → DFM → Process Planning → Tool Selection → Strategy Selection → S/F Optimization → Fusion CAM Creation → Verification → Output Package. MS0 builds the Fusion 360 side of the bridge — the Python endpoints that create CAM operations, extract geometry, and access cloud data.
context_for_cold_start.architecture: TypeScript MCP server (port 3000) ↔ HTTP ↔ Python add-in (port 18360) ↔ adsk.cam/adsk.fusion API. The Python add-in uses a CustomEvent dispatch pattern for thread safety — ALL adsk.* calls MUST run on Fusion's main UI thread. HTTP requests arrive on a daemon thread, get dispatched to main thread via _run_on_main_thread(), results returned to HTTP thread.
critical_rules: ALL adsk.* calls must run on main thread via CustomEvent dispatch — NEVER call from HTTP thread
Fusion 360 internal units are CENTIMETERS — always divide mm values by 10 when passing to adsk API
adsk.doEvents() must be called after geometry/CAM operations to let kernel regenerate
time.sleep() on main thread causes DEADLOCK — never use it
CORS restricted to localhost:3000 — do not open to *
ThreadedHTTPServer (not HTTPServer) — allows /health during long operations

units.title: POST /cam/setup — Create CAM setup with stock, WCS, model bodies
units.intent: After this unit, PRISM can create a new CAM setup in Fusion 360 via HTTP. A machinist opens a model, and PRISM can programmatically set up the manufacturing workspace with correct stock, WCS origin, and model body selection — the first step of any CNC programming workflow.
knowledge_before: READ fusion360_api_server.py lines 147-212 — understand _FusionAPILogic class and dispatch pattern
READ fusion360_api_server.py lines 1247-1413 — existing CAM helper methods (_find_setup, _get_cam_setups, etc.)
Fusion 360 CAM API: adsk.cam.CAM.cast(app.activeProduct) gets CAM product
cam.setups.createInput(adsk.cam.OperationTypes.MillingOperation) creates setup input
setup_input.models = ObjectCollection of BRepBodies (by index from root.bRepBodies)
cam.setups.add(setup_input) finalizes the setup
setup.parameters.itemByName('stock_mode') — set stock type
setup.parameters.itemByName('stock_size_width/height/depth') — set dimensions (IN CM!)

implementation.step_1: Add '/cam/setup': self._create_cam_setup to dispatch dict in _dispatch_post() at line ~196
implementation.step_2: Add method _create_cam_setup(self, body) to _FusionAPILogic class, BEFORE _select_edges method

request_body.name: string — setup name (default: 'PRISM-Setup-1')
request_body.model_body_indices: number[] — indices into root.bRepBodies (default: [0] = first body)

implementation.key_code_pattern:
app = adsk.core.Application.get()
cam = adsk.cam.CAM.cast(app.activeProduct)
if not cam: return {'error': 'No CAM product. Switch to MANUFACTURE workspace.'}
setup_type_map = {'milling': adsk.cam.OperationTypes.MillingOperation, 'turning': adsk.cam.OperationTypes.TurningOperation}
setup_input = cam.setups.createInput(setup_type_map.get(body.get('type','milling'), adsk.cam.OperationTypes.MillingOperation))
# Assign model bodies from indices
design = adsk.fusion.Design.cast(app.activeProduct)
root = design.rootComponent
models = adsk.core.ObjectCollection.create()
for idx in body.get('model_body_indices', [0]):
    if idx < root.bRepBodies.count:
        models.add(root.bRepBodies.item(idx))
setup_input.models = models
new_setup = cam.setups.add(setup_input)
# Set stock parameters via setup.parameters
# REMEMBER: all dimensions must be divided by 10 (mm → cm)

exit_criteria: POST /cam/setup creates a real Fusion CAM setup visible in the browser tree
Stock dimensions set correctly (verify by reading back via GET /cam/setup/stock)
Model bodies correctly assigned (verify via GET /cam/setup/bodies)
Works for both milling and turning setup types
Returns error gracefully when no document is open or no CAM workspace exists
edge_cases: No active document → return {error: 'No active document'}
Active product is not CAM → return {error: 'Switch to MANUFACTURE workspace'}
model_body_indices out of range → skip invalid indices, warn in response
Multiple bodies → all selected bodies appear in setup
Setup name already exists → Fusion auto-increments (Setup1, Setup2, etc.)

four_loop.build: Write the endpoint. Run: python -c "import py_compile; py_compile.compile('fusion360_api_server.py', doraise=True)" → SYNTAX OK
four_loop.scrutinize: Review: thread safety (all adsk.* on main thread), unit conversion (mm→cm), error handling (try/except), CORS (localhost:3000 only)
four_loop.gap_fill: Test: deploy to Fusion AddIns dir, restart add-in, curl POST /cam/setup with test body. Verify setup appears in Fusion browser.
four_loop.tie_up: No TODOs, no stubs, docstring complete, response matches schema, deployed copy matches source

units.title: POST /cam/operation — Create operations with 25+ type mapping
units.intent: After this unit, PRISM can create any of 25+ CAM operation types (face mill, adaptive clear, pocket, contour, drill, bore, thread, slot, etc.) inside a Fusion 360 CAM setup via HTTP. Each operation gets correct parameters with mm→cm conversion. This is the most critical endpoint — without it, AutoProgram cannot generate programs.
knowledge_before: READ CAMKernelEngine.ts — OperationType enum (face_mill, pocket_2d, contour_2d, adaptive_clear, etc.)
Fusion 360 creates operations via: setup.createOperationInput('commandString') where commandString maps to Fusion's internal operation names
Key Fusion command strings: 'face', 'pocket2d', 'contour2d', 'adaptive', 'drill', 'chamfer2d', 'thread', 'bore', 'slot', 'contour3d', 'parallel', 'scallop', 'pencil', 'swarf', 'multiAxisContour'
Parameters set via: operation.parameters.itemByName('tool_spindleSpeed').expression = '4000'
Feed parameters: 'tool_feedCutting' (feed in cm/min — divide mm/min by 10!)
Depth parameters: 'maximumStepdown' (in cm), 'maximumStepover' (in cm)

implementation.step_1: Add OPERATION_TYPE_MAP dict at module level (after PORT = 18360): maps PRISM types to Fusion command strings

request_body.setup_name: string — target setup name (or use setup_index)
request_body.operation_type: string — PRISM operation type from map above

parameters.feed_cutting_mm_min: number — feed rate (DIVIDE BY 10 for Fusion cm/min)

Invalid operation type returns clear error message
Works with setup found by name or index

Setup not found → return {error: 'Setup not found'}
Parameter name doesn't exist for this op type → skip silently, log warning
createOperationInput fails → try fallback via /execute with generated Python

four_loop.scrutinize: Review: mm→cm conversion factors correct (0.1 for all lengths), RPM stays 1.0, error handling per parameter

units.title: POST /cam/assign-tool — Tool assignment from library or inline
units.intent: After this unit, PRISM can assign cutting tools to CAM operations — either by finding a matching tool in Fusion's library or creating one inline from PRISM's tool spec. Without tools, operations are empty shells that can't generate toolpaths.
knowledge_before: Fusion 360 tool assignment: operation.tool = adsk.cam.Tool object
Tools can come from library (existing) or be created inline
adsk.cam.Tool.createFromJson(json_string) creates a tool from JSON spec
Tool JSON format: {"type": "flat end mill", "geometry": {"DC": 10, "LCF": 30, "OAL": 75, "NOF": 3}, ...}
FusionToolExportEngine.ts has the convert_tool() function showing the full JSON schema
Existing /tool-library/search endpoint can find tools in Fusion libraries
Existing /tool-import endpoint can import tools — reuse its tool JSON format

request_body.operation_name: string — name of operation to assign tool to

tool_spec.type: string — 'flat end mill' | 'ball end mill' | 'bull nose end mill' | 'drill' | 'tap' | 'face mill'

request_body.search_library_first: boolean — try to find matching tool in Fusion library before creating (default: true)

exit_criteria: Tool assigned to operation (verify: operation.tool is not None)
Tool diameter matches spec (within ±0.01mm)
Flute count matches spec
If search_library_first=true: prefers existing library tool over inline creation
If no library match: creates tool from spec via Tool.createFromJson()

four_loop.scrutinize: Review: tool JSON schema matches FusionToolExportEngine output, diameter in mm not cm
four_loop.gap_fill: Test: assign endmill, drill, face mill to operations

edge_cases: Tool not in any Fusion library → create inline from spec
Wrong tool type for operation → warn but assign
Insert tool vs solid tool → different JSON schema
Multiple tools with same diameter → pick by flute count match

units.title: POST /cam/toolpath + POST /cam/post — Async toolpath generation + G-code post-processing
units.intent: After this unit, PRISM can trigger toolpath generation (which takes 5-60+ seconds) with async polling, and post-process the result to G-code. This completes the full CAM creation pipeline: setup → operations → tools → toolpaths → G-code.
knowledge_before: cam.generateToolpath(operation) returns GenerateToolpathFuture (async!)
cam.generateAllToolpaths(False) generates for all operations (False = don't prompt user)
future.isGenerationCompleted — poll this for completion
Toolpath gen can take 5-60+ seconds — DO NOT block the HTTP thread
CRITICAL: Cannot use time.sleep() on main thread — use a job tracking pattern instead
Post-processing: adsk.cam.PostProcessInput.createInput(cps_path, program_name, output_folder, unit_option)
cam.postProcess(setup_or_operation, post_input) — generates G-code file
CPS files available at: H:/prism/BOX/FUSION BASIC POSTS/ (150+ files)

implementation.architecture: Use a background job pattern: POST /cam/toolpath fires generation and returns a job_id immediately. GET /cam/toolpath/status?job_id=X polls completion. The GenerateToolpathFuture is stored in a module-level dict _cam_jobs.

exit_criteria: POST /cam/toolpath returns immediately with job_id (not blocking)
GET /cam/toolpath/status reports 'generating' then 'complete'
Toolpath generation completes without crash for face + pocket operations
POST /cam/post generates G-code file at specified output path
G-code output for at least Fanuc and Haas controller dialects
Timeout handling: if generation exceeds 180s, status reports 'timeout'
edge_cases: No operations with tools → error before generation
CPS file not found → clear error with path attempted
Output folder doesn't exist → create it or error
Polling a completed/expired job_id → return cached result or 'expired'

four_loop.build: Write both endpoints + job tracking dict. Syntax check.
four_loop.scrutinize: Review: no time.sleep() on main thread, job dict has max size limit, timeout at 180s
four_loop.gap_fill: Test: generate toolpath for simple face+pocket, post to Fanuc CPS
four_loop.tie_up: Deployed, job tracking cleaned up after 5 min TTL

units.title: GET /cam/geometry-detail — Face-level B-Rep extraction
units.intent: After this unit, PRISM can read the 3D model's topology face-by-face — surface types (plane, cylinder, cone, sphere, torus, NURBS), normals, radii, areas. This is the raw data that FeatureRecognitionEngine needs to classify holes, pockets, slots, and bosses.
knowledge_before: Existing /geometry endpoint (line ~300) returns only aggregate metrics (body count, volume, bounding box)
adsk.fusion.BRepFace: face.geometry gives the surface type (Plane, Cylinder, Cone, Sphere, Torus, NurbsSurface)
adsk.core.Plane: normal vector. adsk.core.Cylinder: radius, axis. adsk.core.Cone: halfAngle.
face.isParamReversed — indicates concavity (True = hole, False = boss for cylinders)
face.area — in cm², multiply by 100 for mm²
face.boundingBox — min/max points in cm
exit_criteria: Every face in the model enumerated with correct surface type
Planar faces have normal vectors
Cylindrical faces have radius + axis + is_hole flag
All units in mm (converted from cm)
Tested on at least 1 BOX part (CASING WITH SINGLE SIDE BORE.step)

four_loop.scrutinize: Review: unit conversion (cm→mm), surface type classification completeness, error handling for complex geometry
four_loop.gap_fill: Test on bracket.step and CASING.step from reference parts

edge_cases: NURBS surfaces → type=nurbs, no normal/radius
Zero-area faces → skip
Assembly with multiple components → enumerate all
Coplanar faces → may share normal but different positions

units.title: GET /cam/feature-candidates — Topology-based feature grouping
units.intent: After this unit, PRISM can identify manufacturing features (holes, pockets, bosses, faces) from raw B-Rep geometry. The output matches FeatureRecognitionEngine's RecognizedFeature[] schema, so it can be fed directly into the AutoProgram pipeline's Stage 2.
knowledge_before: READ FeatureRecognitionEngine.ts first 100 lines — RecognizedFeature interface and FeatureType enum

Feature types: through_hole, blind_hole, counterbore, countersink, tapped_hole, pocket_rectangular, pocket_circular, slot_through, slot_blind, keyway, boss_circular, boss_rectangular, fillet, chamfer, face, step, groove, thread_external, contour_2d
Grouping logic: cylindrical faces with same axis → hole candidate. Through vs blind determined by face loop analysis.
Planar faces at same Z-level → pocket floor candidate
Convex cylinders → boss candidate

features.face_indices: number[] — which faces comprise this feature

units.title: Retry + timeout + health monitoring in Fusion360LiveBridgeEngine.ts
units.intent: After this unit, the TypeScript→Python HTTP bridge is resilient to transient failures. If Python crashes or the network glitches, the TS side retries with exponential backoff instead of failing immediately. This prevents AutoProgram from dying mid-pipeline due to a single HTTP hiccup.
knowledge_before: READ Fusion360LiveBridgeEngine.ts — current HTTP client with AbortController timeout
Current pattern: single fetch() call with 30s timeout, no retry
Need: exponential backoff (100ms, 500ms, 2000ms), per-stage timeout config, health check before pipeline

changes: Add retry wrapper: retryFetch(url, options, maxRetries=3, backoffMs=[100,500,2000])
Add per-stage timeout map: {geometry: 30000, toolpath: 180000, post: 60000, default: 30000}
Add healthCheck() method: GET /health with 5s timeout, returns boolean
Add isConnected property: caches health check result for 10s

exit_criteria: 3 retries with exponential backoff on transient HTTP failures
Per-stage timeout correctly applied (geometry: 30s, toolpath: 180s)
healthCheck() returns true when Python add-in is running
Bridge survives 1 simulated network failure without crashing
edge_cases: Python process crash → all 3 retries fail → return connection error
Network timeout on retry 2 → retry 3 succeeds → return result
Health check fails → isConnected=false → pipeline refuses to start
Concurrent health checks → deduplicate, return cached result

four_loop.build: Add retry wrapper + health check to Fusion360LiveBridgeEngine.ts. tsc --noEmit.
four_loop.scrutinize: Backoff timing correct (100/500/2000ms). No infinite retry loop.
four_loop.gap_fill: Simulate: stop Python add-in, verify retries fire, restart, verify recovery.
four_loop.tie_up: TypeScript compiles clean. Retry + health tested.
